key_insight: In the fixed-parameter, expanding-depth QAOA regime, much of the optimization benefit appears to survive even when entanglement is aggressively removed.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a low-memory, classical QUBO solver can approximate strong MaxCut performance at large scale without per-instance tuning, making it attractive for practical optimization pipelines.
method: Train a compact two-parameter QAOA schedule on small instances, then reuse it as problem size and depth increase.
Use approximate matrix product state simulations up to 50 qubits and 100 layers to track entanglement via bond dimension.
Create BOND-1 by projecting the circuit state onto a product-state manifold after every two-qubit interaction.
evidence_signal: On standard GSet MaxCut benchmarks up to 20,000 variables, BOND-1 reaches cut ratios above 0.95 relative to the best known values and sometimes matches them.
watch_item: The conclusion is regime-specific: these results do not imply entanglement is unimportant for quantum optimization in general.
paper_title: Disentangling QAOA: From Weakly Entangled Circuits to a Classical QUBO Solver
